adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError when i.content is nil (RSS 2.0 description-only or Atom summary feeds), and with retry: false the scheduled job dies permanently and silently with no alert or logging
poll_feed.rb: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no error handling, so one network failure or 500 response on the feed URL permanently kills the feed polling job

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is executed without any `rescue`/timeout handling. `open-uri` can raise on network errors, timeouts, or non-2xx responses, which will bubble up and cause the scheduled Sidekiq job to fail. Additionally `sidekiq_options retry: false` means that failed run will not be retried immediately. However, the claim that it "permanently" kills feed polling is overstated—scheduled jobs would typically run again on the next recurrence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only verifies poll_feed is called, never that it survives a bad feed — the job's failure surface is unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Jobs::PollFeed` and a corresponding spec. The proposed finding is about test coverage: `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` asserts preconditions and that `poll_feed` is delegated to, but does not test behavior when the feed is malformed/unreachable or when `SimpleRSS.parse(open(...))` raises. That is true, but it’s not a concrete defect in the production code introduced by the diff—it's a suggestion to add more robustness tests rather than identifying a real bug/security/correctness issue in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:50: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence check, crashing with NoMethodError on nil when embed_by_username is blank but embeddable_host is set

topic_embed.rb:24-31: TopicEmbed is not destroyed when its topic or post is deleted (no dependent: :destroy), causing EmbedController#best to raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound and return a permanent 500 for that embed URL

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces TopicEmbed as a standalone table with no foreign keys and no cleanup behavior tied to Topic/Post deletion. TopicEmbed only has `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` (which does not imply dependent cleanup); and there are no corresponding `has_one/has_many ... dependent:` associations shown on Topic or Post. EmbedController#best trusts `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (a raw `pluck(:topic_id)`) and, if present, instantiates `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without verifying the topic still exists. If a topic (or its first post) is deleted while the TopicEmbed row remains, `topic_id_for_embed` can return an orphaned topic_id, and TopicView construction is very likely to raise (e.g., RecordNotFound), resulting in a 500 for that embed_url.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb: update path does PostRevisor.new(embed.post) with a nil post after post deletion, causing NoMethodError inside the hourly PollFeed job

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path (the `else` branch when an existing TopicEmbed is found), it does `post = embed.post` and then, if the content hash changed, unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!`. There is no guard for `embed.post` being nil (e.g., if the referenced post was deleted or the association is otherwise broken). In that case, passing nil into PostRevisor would raise at runtime, and Jobs::PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import for each feed item, so an orphaned TopicEmbed would crash the hourly poll job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:18-19: feed_key is defined but never used — the Last-Modified feed-deduplication logic was never implemented, so every run re-downloads and re-processes every feed item

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` (lines ~18-19) computes a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but nothing in `execute` or `poll_feed` ever references it. The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items` every run, so there is no implemented Last-Modified/ETag (or other) feed-level dedup/throttling using that key; the defined method is dead code and the job will re-download the feed and re-check all items each time it runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:41-44: perform_retrieve invokes the full PollFeed inline on every embed request of an unknown URL, so N unknown embed URLs trigger N full feed re-fetches within the throttle window

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the embed URL is not already present (lines shown around the `if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` block). The only throttle in TopicRetriever is `retrieved_recently?`, which is keyed by the specific `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), not globally. Therefore, N distinct unknown embed URLs requested within 60 seconds can each pass the per-URL throttle and each synchronously trigger a full PollFeed run (including `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterating/importing all items), causing repeated feed refetches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_top_topics.rb migration: changing an already-committed migration to use force: true silently drops the existing top_topics table in environments where the table exists but the migration hasn't run, causing data loss

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will DROP the table if it already exists and then recreate it. That introduces a clear data-loss risk in any environment where `top_topics` exists at the time this migration is executed (e.g., created manually, created by a different/older migration/branch, or a partially migrated DB). The finding correctly describes this behavior and risk grounded in the change shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_topic_embeds migration also uses force: true, which can silently drop the table

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` does `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails this will drop the existing `topic_embeds` table (and its data) if it already exists, then recreate it. Since this is a migration (not schema.rb), using `force: true` is unnecessary and introduces a real risk of accidental data loss if the migration is re-run or if a table with that name already exists in an environment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:60-77: absolutize_urls only handles leading-slash URLs, so protocol-relative (//cdn.example.com/...) and bare-relative (images/foo.jpg) URLs pass through unchanged and render broken inside the embedded topic

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links and images are rewritten only when href/src is present and starts_with?('/'). Protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/x" and document-relative URLs like "images/foo.jpg" do not start with '/', so they are left unchanged. Since imported RSS/Readability HTML can contain these forms, the method does not fully “absolutize” relative URLs and can result in broken resources/links when rendering the imported post in Discourse.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:23-29: when content_sha1 changes, only the post body is revised — the topic title is never updated, leaving stale titles on edited articles

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the creation path passes `title:` to `PostCreator`, so the topic title is initially set. However, in the update path (`else` branch) when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it only calls `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, ...)`, and that method signature in this diff (`revise!(user, new_raw, opts = {})`) only revises the post body (raw/cooked) and does not take or apply a new title. The `title` argument passed into `TopicEmbed.import` is ignored on updates. Therefore, if an imported article’s title changes (and even if the body changes), the Discourse topic title will remain stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/loading.html.erb: no terminal failure state — if retrieval permanently fails, the page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with an infinite 'Loading Discussion...' spinner and no error surfaced to the embedding site

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `embed/loading`. The `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` template unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds. There is no max retry count, timeout, or error path; if retrieval never succeeds (e.g., job fails, remote fetch/parse fails, settings/user missing), the iframe will keep reloading and showing “Loading Discussion...” indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:15-21: unique index race on TopicEmbed.create! — concurrent imports of the same URL (controller path vs PollFeed) raise unrescued ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, crashing the job and rolling back the topic

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-insert: it queries `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank, later calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so two concurrent imports of the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on `create!`. There is no rescue around this, so the exception will bubble up and fail the caller (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` which calls `TopicEmbed.import` directly, and has `sidekiq_options retry: false`), and the surrounding `Topic.transaction` will roll back the topic/post created by `PostCreator` in that transaction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb:48-53: the success rendering path mocks TopicView, so best.html.erb (including nil user and blank posts branches) has never been executed by any test

adjudication.rationale: The cited lines in `embed_controller_spec.rb` do stub/mock `TopicView.new`, and RSpec controller specs typically do not render views unless `render_views` is enabled, so `best.html.erb` may indeed not be executed in these tests. However, this is a test-coverage observation, not a verifiable defect/bug/security/correctness problem introduced in the production code by the diff. The diff does not show a failing or incorrect behavior; it only shows that the controller spec doesn’t exercise the view logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec covers the 'retrieval fails' flow for the embed loading view

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an embed feature with a `loading` view rendered when no `topic_id` is found (and a job is enqueued). The included specs cover: missing `embed_url`, missing/invalid host/referer, and the branches where `topic_id_for_embed` is nil vs present. There is no explicit “retrieval fails” branch implemented in the code (no error handling/state for job failure), so the finding is essentially about test coverage for a hypothetical failure scenario rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated rewrite of the Disqus import task in lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-141 removes the --category CLI option and drops created_at, causing imported Disqus topics to lose category targeting and be stamped with import time instead of the original thread date

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes `method_option :category` entirely and deletes all logic that looks up `category_id` and passes `category: category_id` to `PostCreator`. It also replaces the `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` do not accept or set `created_at` (they call `PostCreator.new` without `created_at`), so the created topic/post will default to the import time rather than the original thread date. Both behavior regressions are directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Modification of existing applied migration db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adds force: true, which drops the existing top_topics table and destroys all its rows if the migration is ever re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before recreating it (typically `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics`), which would destroy any existing rows if this migration is applied against a database where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., if migrations are re-run or the migration is executed on a DB missing the corresponding schema_migrations entry). Without `force: true`, Rails would instead raise an error when the table exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js in app/assets/javascripts/ is never servable or distributed: the diff contains no route, precompile-list addition, or documented include path, making the embed feature unusable as shipped

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, but assets under `app/assets` are generally served via the Rails asset pipeline and do not require an explicit route. Also, the embed JS is plausibly intended to be included by an external site (not necessarily referenced from within this Rails app), so the absence of an in-app include path in the diff does not, by itself, prove the feature is unusable. Whether `embed.js` (and similarly `embed.css` referenced by `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`) must be added to a production precompile list depends on existing asset configuration not shown in the diff, so the claim that it is “never servable or distributed” is not verifiable from this change alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22: feed_key is defined but never referenced, pointing maintainers at a caching invariant that does not exist

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, a `feed_key` method is defined (building a Redis key from `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`), but `poll_feed` and `execute` never call `feed_key`, and there is no other reference to `feed_key` anywhere in the provided diff. This makes it dead/unused code in this change, which can mislead maintainers into thinking a caching/throttling mechanism exists for feed polling when it does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead client locale entry in config/locales/client.en.yml:1477 adds 'embedding' to the client-side admin settings category list but no corresponding site settings have client: true, leaving an unrenderable UI string

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `embedding:` category to `config/site_settings.yml` with four settings (`embeddable_host`, `feed_polling_enabled`, `feed_polling_url`, `embed_by_username`). The added client locale key `admin_js.site_settings.categories.embedding` will be used to label that category in the admin UI. The fact that none of these settings are marked `client: true` does not make the string “unrenderable”; `client: true` controls exposure to the public client, not whether the admin settings UI can render a category/setting. Therefore this is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated whitespace churn in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb (trailing-whitespace fixup and removal of trailing newline) pollutes the history of an unrelated pre-existing migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include whitespace-only changes in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb (removal of trailing spaces on a blank line and the file now lacks a trailing newline, as indicated by "No newline at end of file"). However, this is purely formatting/whitespace churn and does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the migration logic—it's a style/history cleanliness nit rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External untrusted HTML from feed content is stored and rendered as raw cooked content with no sanitization, enabling arbitrary script execution from a compromised feed (XSS)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an RSS/Atom import path that stores and renders feed HTML without sanitization. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it takes `i.content` from the feed (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` now returns `raw` directly when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline where sanitization would typically occur. Additionally, the embed view outputs this content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative href/src and does not remove scripts or unsafe attributes. Therefore, a compromised/malicious feed can inject arbitrary HTML/JS leading to XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Even the readability path whitelists tags but keeps href/src attributes verbatim, so javascript: URLs in links survive sanitization

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` pulls arbitrary remote HTML (`doc.content`) allowing ``/`` and `href`/`src` attributes, then `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` and skips the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Nothing in the diff sanitizes or scheme-checks `href`/`src` values (e.g., `javascript:`), and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites leading-`/` URLs, leaving other schemes untouched. Therefore a `javascript:` link in imported content can survive and be served verbatim, enabling XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is computed in PollFeed but never used; the feed-modified check to skip re-parsing unchanged feeds is unimplemented dead code, causing unbounded re-fetching and re-parsing proportional to feed size on a hot path

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined to compute a redis/cache key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the job. `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates every item on every execution, with no "modified"/ETag/Last-Modified check or stored marker to skip unchanged feeds. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, so this full re-fetch/re-parse can occur on the embed retrieval path, not just the hourly schedule. This makes the `feed_key` method dead code and the intended skip-on-unchanged behavior unimplemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: i.content.scrub in PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on standard RSS 2.0 feeds because SimpleRSS leaves content nil for description-based items, and with retry: false the polling job dies silently so no topics are ever imported via polling
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same root bug: calling `i.content.scrub` when `i.content` is nil (common on RSS 2.0 feeds where items use `description` instead of `content`), leading to a NoMethodError/nil dereference. It aligns with the golden comment’s concern and implies the need for a fallback (e.g., to `description`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever synchronously re-runs the entire feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) inline to service a single URL retrieval, doing O(whole feed) work per request with the throttle bypassed for staff users

adjudication.rationale: In TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (not enqueued), which immediately parses the entire configured feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then iterates `rss.items.each`) before continuing. This happens while retrieving a single `@embed_url`, and can be triggered repeatedly because `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` returns `false` when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is set. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` sets `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`, so staff-triggered retrieves bypass the 60s throttle and can synchronously re-run the whole feed poll each time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Every render of loading.html.erb by anonymous visitors enqueues a retrieve_topic job before any throttle check, flooding the Sidekiq queue since the redis throttle only dedups execution, not enqueuing

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists (topic_id is nil), it unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and then renders `loading` (which triggers a reload every 30s). There is no dedupe/throttle on enqueuing, so repeated requests (including from anonymous users where `user_id` is nil) will keep adding `retrieve_topic` jobs to Sidekiq. The only throttle shown (`TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` using Redis) runs when the job executes, so it prevents repeated *retrieval* but does not prevent the queue from being filled with redundant jobs that will later no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 30-second reload loop in loading.html.erb has no terminal state, backoff, or client-side stop condition, so a URL that can never be imported reloads and re-enqueues forever

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` after 30s with no stop condition. If the embed can never be created (e.g., `TopicRetriever` refuses to fetch due to invalid URI/host mismatch in `invalid_host?`, missing `embed_by_username`, fetch failures, etc.), `topic_id_for_embed` will stay nil, so the page will reload indefinitely and each reload will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job. `TopicRetriever` has a 60s throttle for doing work, but it does not prevent repeated job enqueuing or an infinite client reload loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No URL normalization on the embed_url join key between the two ingestion paths (feed link vs discourseEmbedUrl), so discrepancies like trailing slashes, http vs https, or query strings cause permanent lookup misses and duplicate topic imports

adjudication.rationale: The code uses the raw `embed_url` string as the unique join key everywhere (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`; `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`; `topic_id_for_embed` does exact match). There is no canonicalization/normalization step (e.g., scheme normalization http/https, trailing slash removal, fragment stripping, query normalization). Different ingestion/request paths can therefore refer to the same article with different URL forms: `Jobs::PollFeed` imports using `i.link`/`i.id`, while the embed widget hits `/embed/best?embed_url=...` based on `discourseEmbedUrl`, and `TopicRetriever`/`import_remote` import using that URL verbatim. Any mismatch will cause lookup misses and can trigger a second import (duplicate topic) rather than finding the existing `TopicEmbed` row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No dependent: :destroy, FK, or destroy hook for TopicEmbed rows, so deleting the imported post or topic leaves a dangling TopicEmbed; the next feed poll then crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! with NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces TopicEmbed records that reference posts/topics via integer columns (topic_id, post_id) but adds no foreign keys and no `dependent: :destroy` on either side. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is found it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revise!`. If the referenced Post was deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil`, and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` (or subsequent `revise!`/`@post` usage) will raise a NoMethodError. This is a concrete failure mode caused by dangling TopicEmbed rows and is verifiable from the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If the topic is deleted, topic_id_for_embed returns a stale id and TopicView.new raises RecordNotFound, causing a permanent 500 on embed/best for that URL

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is implemented as `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`, which does not verify that the referenced `topics` row still exists. There are no foreign keys or `dependent: :destroy` relationships shown that would guarantee `topic_embeds` rows are removed when a topic is deleted. In `EmbedController#best`, if a `topic_id` is returned it unconditionally calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no rescue/fallback. If the topic was deleted but the `topic_embeds` row remains, this will pass an invalid/stale id into `TopicView`, which in typical Rails/Discourse codepaths will attempt to load the topic and can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, producing a 500 for that embed URL until the stale `topic_embeds` row is cleaned up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Origin check in embed.js uses a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of an origin comparison, so any origin that is a substring of the forum URL passes the check
layouts/embed.html.erb injects request.referer unescaped into a JS string literal as the postMessage targetOrigin
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that `request.referer` is inserted into JavaScript without escaping (in `layouts/embed.html.erb`). The golden frames the risk as XSS via malicious referer content; the candidate describes the same unescaped interpolation context (JS string literal for `postMessage` targetOrigin), which is the same underlying vulnerability vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The raw_html cook path returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently bypassing the documented plugin extension point for imported posts

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns early (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), which skips the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call. Since imported RSS/remote content is explicitly created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in TopicEmbed.import, those posts will never trigger the `:after_post_cook` plugin hook. This is a concrete, behavior-changing bypass of the plugin extension point for those posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The change to PostRevisor at line 85 makes skip_validations bypass all model validations for any caller of the revisor, a global behavioral change to a shared library beyond just the embed path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning callers can now intentionally bypass model validations by passing `skip_validations: true` (as the new `TopicEmbed.import` path does). However, this is an opt-in behavior gated by an internal option, not something automatically applied to all callers, and the change is consistent with the option name/use (similar to `PostCreator` already supporting `skip_validations`). The finding frames this as a defect solely because it’s a shared-library behavior change, but the diff does not show any unintended/unsafe caller path or regression—only a deliberate new capability used by the embed importer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import via TopicEmbed.import_remote silently loses created_at, giving every imported thread the current timestamp and destroying chronological ordering of the archive

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import previously created the topic with `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)`, preserving the Disqus thread timestamp. The diff removes that and replaces it with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which constructs `PostCreator.new(user, title: title, raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` and does not pass `created_at`. Therefore the created topic/post will default to the current time, breaking chronological ordering for imported threads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The -c/--category CLI option was removed from the Disqus import task with no replacement, breaking existing scripts that pass it

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line was removed, along with all logic that reads `options[:category]` and maps it to a `category_id`. Thor will treat `-c/--category` as an unknown option, so any existing scripts/automation invoking `disqus:import` with that flag will now fail. The new implementation (`TopicEmbed.import_remote`) does not provide an alternative way to specify a category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Outbound fetches in TopicRetriever and TopicEmbed use bare open-uri with no explicit timeout, so a slow remote site stalls the RetrieveTopic worker indefinitely and locks out retries for that URL for 60s

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces outbound HTTP fetches via `open-uri` without specifying any timeout options. Specifically, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` and `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. These are invoked from background processing paths (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http` called by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, and the scheduled poller). With no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, a slow/hung remote server can block the worker for an extended period. The finding’s “indefinitely” wording may be stronger than strictly provable (Ruby/Net::HTTP may have defaults), but the core issue—no explicit timeouts on external fetches in worker code—is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsanitized URL interpolated into raw HTML footer in app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 allows stored XSS; the ^https?:// regex validation passes malicious URLs like http://x.com/"><script>alert(1)</script>, which are rendered raw via cook_method: raw_html
The sanitization intent of import_remote (readability tag whitelist) is silently undone by the import method appending the unescaped URL fragment in the same code path

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the fetched article HTML is constrained by Readability’s `tags`/`attributes` lists, but `TopicEmbed.import` then unconditionally appends its own HTML: `"#{url}"` inside the `embed.imported_from` string. The `url` is not HTML-escaped for either the attribute or text. Although `import` enforces `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, that does not prevent attribute/text injection if `url` contains characters like a single quote (used to delimit the href) or other HTML-breaking characters. Thus the sanitization intent can be bypassed by the appended unescaped fragment in the same code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS content path in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 has no sanitization at all; PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import directly bypassing the readability whitelist, so arbitrary HTML including <script> and <iframe> is stored verbatim as cooked and rendered raw, enabling stored XSS from a malicious feed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is taken as `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed to `TopicEmbed.import` without any HTML sanitization/whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. The embed view (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. `scrub` only fixes invalid byte sequences; it does not remove `<script>`, event handlers, iframes, etc. This makes it possible for a malicious/compromised RSS/ATOM feed to store and serve arbitrary HTML/JS (stored XSS) via the imported posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A single malformed feed item permanently blocks the entire feed import: i.content is nil on RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide description, causing NoMethodError on nil.scrub that aborts the loop

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, each item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. With SimpleRSS, RSS 2.0 items commonly expose `description` and may not have a `content` field (it can be nil unless there is content:encoded/Atom content). If `i.content` is nil for any item, calling `.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the job mid-loop and preventing subsequent items from importing; because the scheduled job runs repeatedly and doesn’t rescue per-item, the same bad item can keep failing the whole import until the feed/item changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No per-item rescue in PollFeed combined with sidekiq_options retry: false means one bad item or open() failure prevents all subsequent items from being imported and the job fails silently with no retry every hour forever

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `PollFeed` sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` with no `rescue` around the fetch/parse or around per-item processing (`i.content.scrub`, `TopicEmbed.import`). Any exception (network/open-uri failure, parse error, nil `i.content` causing `NoMethodError`, or an exception from `TopicEmbed.import`) will abort the entire job run and prevent subsequent items from importing in that run. With `retry: false`, Sidekiq will not retry that failed execution (though the scheduled job will run again on the next hourly recurrence). The "fails silently" / "no retry every hour forever" wording is overstated, but the core defect (single failure stops all remaining imports and no Sidekiq retries) is verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw_html cook method in app/models/post.rb:132 bypasses the after_post_cook plugin filter contract, silently skipping all plugins hooking that filter while posts still appear as normal topics in the main forum

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes Post#cook to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call. TopicEmbed.import creates regular posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so these posts will be used like normal posts but will never run the `:after_post_cook` plugin filter, potentially breaking plugins that assume that filter is always invoked for cooked content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import in lib/tasks/disqus.thor silently changed behavior: --category option and original timestamps dropped; new behavior scrapes remote article body, uses current timestamps, and cannot target a category

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes `method_option :category` and all logic that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` to `PostCreator`, so the task can no longer target a category. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote/import` do not set `created_at`, so the imported topic/post will use current timestamps instead of the original thread timestamp. Additionally, the initial post content changes from a simple permalink markdown to scraped remote article content via `ruby-readability`, changing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No failure path in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 with loading view; if retrieval fails no TopicEmbed row is created, so every subsequent request re-enqueues and re-renders 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`. There is no state recorded for a failed/invalid retrieval, so `topic_id_for_embed` will continue to be nil and the controller will keep enqueuing and showing the loading page indefinitely.

This is especially verifiable because `ensure_embeddable` only validates the *referer* host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but does not validate that the `embed_url` param’s host matches. In that case the job runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, where `invalid_host?` will return true (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`) and no retrieval happens, guaranteeing no `TopicEmbed` row is ever created—so the loading view never resolves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view's 30-second setTimeout reload combined with 1-minute response caching means even on success visitors can stare at a reloading 'Loading' screen for up to a minute

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and `render 'loading'`, but the method does not `return` after rendering. As written, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` runs for both the successful and loading responses, so the loading page is cacheable for 60 seconds. The loading template reloads the page every 30 seconds via `setTimeout(document.location.reload(), 30000)`. With a 1-minute cache lifetime, those reloads can repeatedly serve the cached loading response even after the background job has created the topic, meaning visitors may keep seeing the reloading “Loading Discussion...” page until the cache expires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path in app/models/topic_embed.rb:31 crashes on orphaned embeds; posts can be deleted by moderators while topic_embeds row remains, so embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises, killing the whole scheduled poll

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path loads the existing embed via `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, then does `post = embed.post` and, if the SHA1 changed, immediately calls `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb around the else branch). There is no guard for `post` being nil. Since the migration creates `topic_embeds.post_id` without a foreign key and the association has no `dependent:` behavior, it’s possible for a `topic_embeds` row to remain while its referenced post is deleted, making `embed.post` nil and causing `PostRevisor.new(nil)` to raise. This would break scheduled feed polling when it hits such an orphan and a content change triggers the revise path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key method in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19-21 is dead code; the conditional-fetch/Last-Modified caching intent was silently dropped, so the full feed is re-fetched and every item re-processed every hour

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method (lines ~19-21) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it is dead/unreachable code. Additionally, `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on each scheduled run (hourly), with no use of `feed_key` or any conditional HTTP fetch/caching mechanism. It then iterates all `rss.items` every run and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each, meaning the entire feed is fetched and each item is at least re-evaluated each hour (even if `TopicEmbed.import` may avoid duplicating unchanged posts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated modification of already-shipped migration db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb: force: true will silently DROP TABLE any existing top_topics data if run against a database where the table exists outside schema-migrations; appears to be a local-dev hack

In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can destroy existing `top_topics` data in any environment where the table exists but the migration is (re)run (e.g., inconsistent DB state, manual table creation, loading schema then running migrations). This is a potentially destructive behavioral change to a migration and is not just stylistic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only edits to unrelated shipped migration 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb included as churn in the diff

adjudication_records.issue_text: The PR folds in three unacknowledged objective changes (raw_html trust model, Disqus tool rewrite, unrelated migration modifications) beyond its stated 'embed URL handling and validation' objective; items #1, #2, #4 combined constitute a security regression that should block merge until the footer is escaped and both import paths run through a common sanitizer

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` mode and changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` and `import_remote` create/update posts using this raw HTML path (`PostCreator` is passed `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Neither the RSS path (Jobs::PollFeed uses `i.content` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)`) nor the readability path applies a sanitizer, so hostile HTML from feeds/remote pages can be stored and rendered. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` appends an HTML footer containing `url` interpolated into an `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping; the only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quote/attribute injection. These are concrete, verifiable XSS/trust-model regressions introduced by the diff. (The claim about “unacknowledged objective changes” is contextual, but the security issues themselves are real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: Post#cook returns raw content when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing the sanitization pipeline; TopicEmbed.import stores un-sanitized external HTML as post.cooked which is rendered with raw post.cooked in the embed view (app/models/post.rb:131, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:21)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `raw_html` cook method (Post.cook_methods) and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (where Discourse typically sanitizes/normalizes HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from external content (RSS/Readability) using `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so the post’s rendered content can remain untrusted HTML. The embed view then renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, meaning any HTML in `post.cooked` is injected into the page without escaping. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` appends an `<a href='#{url}'>` using single quotes, while the URL is only regex-checked for `^https?://` and could include a single quote payload. Together, this is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed imports feed content with zero HTML filtering: raw RSS content is passed directly to TopicEmbed.import which stores it as raw_html; CGI.unescapeHTML actively decodes entities, re-materializing encoded script tags as live markup (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-33)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In app/models/post.rb, `cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore RSS/Atom-provided HTML is effectively rendered as-is, and `CGI.unescapeHTML` can turn encoded tags (e.g., `<script>`) back into live markup, creating an XSS vector if the feed content is untrusted/compromised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped URL interpolated into a single-quoted href attribute in the imported_from footer with no escaping; the upstream validation regex permits quotes and spaces, enabling attribute-injection stored XSS from feed item links (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which merely enforces an http(s) prefix and does not exclude quotes/spaces. The code then interpolates `url` directly into an HTML string: `"#{url}"` and appends it to `contents`. These imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (and Post#cook returns `raw` for raw_html), and the embed view renders with `raw post.cooked`, so the HTML is not escaped. Therefore a feed item/link like `http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)` would break out of the single-quoted href attribute and become stored XSS in the imported post footer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF via redirect-following defeats the host check: open-uri transparently follows HTTP redirects so an open redirect on the embeddable host lets the server-side fetch pivot to internal services like cloud metadata endpoints; the invalid_host? check never re-runs on redirects (app/models/topic_embed.rb:41-42, lib/topic_retriever.rb:15-17)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new embed import path fetches remote content with `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the retrieval gate in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the host of the originally supplied `@embed_url` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects transparently, so an attacker who can cause a request to a URL on the allowed `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` that 30x-redirects to another host/IP (e.g., internal services or cloud metadata) can bypass the single host check and pivot the server-side fetch to the redirected destination. The host check is not re-evaluated after redirects, making the SSRF vector verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer header used as an authorization gate: Referer is fully client-controlled so any non-browser client can forge it to bypass the embeddable_host check, while also denying legitimate users whose privacy extensions strip Referer (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-28)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` enforces access by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and raises if missing/mismatched (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-28). This is an authorization gate based on the HTTP Referer header, which is not a reliable security control: it may be absent (privacy tools / browser policy), causing legitimate requests to be rejected (also reflected in the controller spec expecting failure with no referer), and it can be forged by non-browser clients, allowing bypass of the intended host restriction when accessing the endpoint outside a browser context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check uses substring matching (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of strict origin equality, allowing origins that are substrings of the configured URL to pass the check (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15)
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: validating postMessage origins via indexOf/substring matching rather than strict origin equality, which can be bypassed by a malicious domain that contains the expected URL as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrations use force: true in create_table, which drops pre-existing tables and risks data loss (db/migrate/20131217233733_create_topic_embeds.rb, 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly uses `force: true` in `create_table` for `topic_embeds` (`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`) and changes `top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`). In Rails, `force: true` drops an existing table before creating it, so if these migrations are run against a DB where the table already exists (e.g., partially applied migrations, reruns, or inconsistent environments), it can cause data loss. The proposed finding’s specific migration filename for topic_embeds is slightly off, but the underlying issue is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability tag/attribute whitelist does not filter URL schemes, so href="javascript:..." attributes survive sanitization

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which uses `ruby-readability` with `attributes: %w[href src]` and then stores `doc.content` into a post created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` and skips the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no additional filtering of `href`/`src` protocols anywhere in `import_remote`/`import`/`absolutize_urls`, so a `href="javascript:..."` (or similar) in the extracted content would be persisted and rendered as-is. Therefore the finding (unsafe URL schemes surviving the readability allowlist) corresponds to a real XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:7 verifies nothing — the request fails because ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess (embeddable_host defaults to '') before params.require(:embed_url) is reached, and Rails returns 400 (ParameterMissing) rather than 404, so the test would pass even if the params.require line were deleted

adjudication.rationale: In the new `EmbedController`, `ensure_embeddable` runs as a `before_filter` and immediately raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. The site setting default added in this diff is `embeddable_host: ''`, so in the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url"` (which does not stub `embeddable_host` or `referer`) the request will fail in the filter before the action executes `params.require(:embed_url)`. Because the assertion is only `response.should_not be_success`, the test will pass regardless of whether `params.require(:embed_url)` exists or not, so it does not actually verify the intended missing-parameter behavior (and it doesn't assert 404 at all).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' test (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-44) only asserts that a mock was constructed; render_views is not declared so best.html.erb is never rendered and the endpoint's actual output (best-of-5 post selection, fallback rendering, header/footer output) is never checked

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec does only assert that `TopicView.new` is invoked with expected arguments, and RSpec controller specs typically do not render views unless `render_views` is enabled. However, this is a test coverage critique (the spec doesn’t verify rendered HTML/output), not a defect in the application logic introduced by the diff. Nothing in the diff indicates the endpoint is incorrect; the test is intentionally mocking/stubbing dependencies and checking controller behavior at that level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:17-27) don't isolate their conditions — neither stubs feed_polling_enabled?, which defaults to false, so poll_feed is never called and both tests would pass even if the .present? checks were deleted

In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” examples only stub feed_polling_url or embed_by_username to nil, but do not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. Since the default in config/site_settings.yml sets feed_polling_enabled: false, the first condition will already short-circuit and prevent poll_feed from running. Therefore both tests would still pass even if the .present? checks for feed_polling_url or embed_by_username were removed, meaning they don’t actually verify those conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The entire poll_feed body (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:22-35) is untested — the url fallback to i.id when blank or non-http, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), the user.blank? early return, and delegation to TopicEmbed.import are never executed because the delegation test stubs poll_feed itself

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` with non-trivial logic in `poll_feed` (user lookup and early return, parsing via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, URL fallback to `i.id`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and calling `TopicEmbed.import`). adjudication_records.issue_text: The valid-host tests in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32-43 stub all real logic and verify only mock orchestration — the 60-second Redis throttle, no_throttle staff bypass, existing-embed bail-out, PollFeed-first path, and fetch_http's user lookup are never exercised

This means none of `retrieved_recently?`’s real Redis throttling behavior (setnx/expire), the `no_throttle` bypass, nor `perform_retrieve`’s internal paths (existing-embed early return, PollFeed-first behavior, or `fetch_http`’s user lookup and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` call) are exercised by these tests. adjudication_records.issue_text: The change-detection branch in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:41-44 is only tested on its true side — no test imports identical content a second time, so the sha1 comparison's no-op path (preventing redundant revisions) is unverified and deleting the condition would not fail any test

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, the only re-import test (“Supports updating the post”) changes the contents, so it exercises the `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` branch in TopicEmbed.import. There is no test that imports the same URL with identical `contents` a second time and asserts no revision occurs (e.g., no PostRevisor invoked / raw unchanged / updated_at unchanged). Therefore the sha1 no-op path is unverified, and removing the condition would not be caught by the current spec suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote's Readability path (topic_embed.rb:38-47) is untested by any test in the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (topic_embed.rb) which uses `ruby-readability` + `open(url)` and then delegates to `TopicEmbed.import`. The added specs cover `TopicEmbed.import` (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) and controller/retriever/feed polling behavior, but none invoke `TopicEmbed.import_remote` or stub its HTTP/readability behavior. adjudication_records.issue_text: The non-80/443 port-prefix branch of absolutize_urls (topic_embed.rb:61) is untested by any test in the diff

adjudication_records.issue_text: Destructive edit to already-shipped migration: `force: true` added to create_top_topics.rb will drop the existing top_topics table without backup when re-run (db:reset, restore-then-migrate, partially-failed db:migrate:reset), silently destroying all top-topic data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an old migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` *would* drop an existing `top_topics` table if this migration were executed against a DB where that table already exists, Rails migrations are not normally “re-run” once recorded in `schema_migrations`. In the scenarios cited (e.g., `db:reset`, restore-then-migrate with a clean schema), the database is dropped/recreated so there is no existing table/data to be silently destroyed. Therefore the finding hinges on atypical/inconsistent DB states (table exists but migration is being executed), which is speculative rather than a verifiable problem introduced by the diff in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` on new production table topic_embeds in create_topic_embeds.rb: if topic_embeds exists with rows from a partial application or halfway deploy, the migration silently DROPs it, irrecoverably losing the embed_url-to-topic mapping, content_sha1 change-tracking state, and requiring re-crawling to regenerate

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails this will drop the existing `topic_embeds` table (and its rows) if it already exists, then recreate it. That is a data-loss risk if the table exists for any reason (e.g., a previously/partially applied deploy, manual creation, or a failed migration on a DB where DDL isn’t rolled back), and it would wipe the embed_url/topic mapping and `content_sha1` state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds table references topics.id and posts.id with plain integer columns (no foreign key, no ON DELETE) and no destroy hook on the topic side, so topic/post deletion permanently orphans topic_embeds rows

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` integer columns and only adds a unique index on `embed_url`; it does not add DB foreign keys or ON DELETE cascades. However, the finding’s conclusion that deletions will “permanently orphan” rows (and that there is “no destroy hook on the topic side”) is not verifiable from this diff: deletion behavior and any cleanup hooks/callbacks in `Topic`/`Post` are not shown, and the project may intentionally not use DB-level FKs. So the concrete, verifiable fact (no FK constraints) is true, but the asserted defect (guaranteed orphaning) is speculative based on code outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Orphaned topic_embeds rows cause EmbedController#best to 500 on the publisher's page by calling TopicView.new on a dead topic_id

Orphaned topic_embeds rows permanently poison the embed URL: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve bails on TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?, the unique index blocks re-import, and TopicEmbed.import takes the update branch and crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil) since embed.post is nil

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import` which assumes an existing `TopicEmbed` row always has an associated `post` (`post = embed.post`). There is no foreign key constraint and no `dependent: ...` behavior shown to prevent `topic_embeds.post_id` from pointing to a deleted/missing post. In that case, when content changes (`content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`), the update path will execute `PostRevisor.new(post)` with `post == nil`, which would raise (since `PostRevisor` expects a Post). Separately, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` returns early if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so a broken/orphaned `topic_embeds` row would prevent automatic re-retrieval for that URL (“poisoning” it). This is a concrete failure mode implied by the code as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:29 unconditionally persists the new content_sha1 via update_column even when the PostRevisor revise! failed or returned false, so future polls skip the revision and source article changes are never synced to the post with no error surfaced

Post#cook reads the new cook_method column in the same release that adds it via add_cook_method_to_posts migration, with no expand phase: during a rolling deploy where a process runs new code against an unmigrated schema, every post creation raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid/MissingAttributeError, breaking the whole forum

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new NOT NULL `cook_method` column via `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`, and immediately changes runtime code to call `cook_method`/`cook_method=` (e.g., `Post#cook` does `return raw if cook_method == ...`, and `PostCreator#setup_post` does `post.cook_method = ...`). In a rolling deploy where some app servers run this new code before the migration has been applied, the `posts` table will not have the `cook_method` column, so ActiveRecord will not define `cook_method` accessors and these calls will raise (typically `NoMethodError` / missing attribute method), breaking cooking and potentially post creation/updates. This is a real backward-compatibility issue between code and schema in the same release with no expand/contract phase.
